Some of it won\'t play on this version of the app (those bits are skipped):

A kit picks the instruments. The app still writes the music: the kit only decides what each part sounds like.

The parts: mel (the melody), bass, pad (the chords) and drums. A part you leave out plays the normal (Classic) sound.

A kit is a text file named kit.txt. The smallest one is two lines:

title: My First Kit
mel: engine modal, modal bell, level 6

Each part gets one line: its name, a colon, then settings separated by commas. "engine" picks the instrument: pluck, bowed, modal (bell, marimba, bowl), analog (a synth), sub (an 808 bass), drums, chip (an old game console), chop, or sample (your own recordings). "level" sets the volume.

Your own recordings: put kit.txt and the sound files in one folder and use Import kit folder.
• As drums, a recording plays just as you recorded it (good for knocks, squeaks and claps):
drums: engine sample, kick knock.wav, snare squeak.wav, hat keys.wav
• As melody, bass or pad, the band plays it at different notes. Write the note it already is after the file name (C4 is middle C, or leave it out):
mel: engine sample, sample chime.wav C5

Lines starting with # are notes to yourself. If something is mistyped, the import report says which setting was skipped.

The full step-by-step guide, with every instrument and setting, is docs/MAKING-KITS.md in the app's GitHub repository (dadcraftttv/Ouralia).

Sound only ever plays to headphones; if they are unplugged the audio stops. Changing a device restarts the audio for a moment. A Bluetooth headset used as the input switches to the low-quality call mode; for the best sound use the phone or a wired mic as input and Bluetooth only for output.

Android sees your wired earbuds as headphones with no microphone, so their mic cannot be chosen. Unplug them and push the plug in all the way (a half-seated plug looks like plain headphones), and check that the plug has two black bands, not one. Until then, the phone\'s mic is used.
This headset\'s mic works in call mode: mono and low quality, and the sound in your ears drops to call quality too. Unless your earbuds support LE Audio, the phone\'s mic gives a much better result.
LE Audio headset: its mic should sound far better than ordinary Bluetooth call mode. If it sounds thin or muffled, switch the input back to the phone\'s mic.

Realm Hopper: hop between Realms to fit what is happening around you

Each Realm fades the sliders to the preset you pick when its situation lasts a few seconds. When none applies, your own settings fade back. Locked sliders stay put, and so does any group a realm is set not to change. Only for the built-in effects, not scenes.

This app listens to the world around you and turns it into music, live, in your headphones.

It can echo and glitch what it hears, build a beat from the knocks and claps around you, play melodies and harmonies in key, answer a note you hum, and change its sound to fit where you are and how you move.

A few short pages and a quick tour, then you're ready.

The app only plays into headphones or earbuds, never the phone\'s speaker: the microphone would hear the speaker and it would screech.\n\nWired headphones work best (the least delay). Bluetooth works too, but most Bluetooth headsets can only use their own mic in phone-call quality, so the phone\'s own mic usually sounds better.

The app needs the microphone to hear the world around you.\n\nWhat it hears is played back live and never saved to a file or sent anywhere. Sounds it catches for its beats and melodies are kept in memory only, and are gone when you stop.

When you press Start you'll hear only the world around you through your headphones, with nothing added. Everything is switched off.

That's on purpose: turn one thing on, listen to what it does, then try the next. A few places to begin:

• Sound tab: Echo level, then the effects below it.
• The Band tab: Rhythm (Beat level) and Music (switch it on).
• Realms tab: Realm Hopper, which change the sound by themselves to fit where you are.

Clap, knock, talk, hum a note, walk around, and hear how each one answers.

Next, a short tour on the real screen: what the small buttons do, then you'll switch on your first effect and hear it change your voice, live.

The screen dims while a note is showing, and only the part it points at can be touched. Tap Next to go on, or Skip tour at any time.

You can see all this again under Setup, About.
Presets keep the sounds you make. Tap Presets for your list. The small buttons beside it:
Save: keeps the sound you have now as a preset, under a name you choose.
Export: saves a preset as a small file, to keep as a backup or send to a friend.
Import: loads a preset file someone sent you.
Stuck for ideas? These change many sliders at once.
Randomize: every slider jumps somewhere new (while the sound plays it glides there).
Nudge: every slider moves a little, for a sound close to this one.
Undo: back to the sound before.
Movers: lets the card\'s sliders move by themselves, with your steps, the sound around you or the way you hold the phone.
On/off switch: turns the effect on or off without losing its settings.
Open: tap the heading to show the sliders. The app remembers which cards you opened.
Always at the bottom, in reach of your thumb.
Start / Stop: the sound on or off.
Now playing: what\'s happening, and why. Tap it for the Intensity dial (calmer to the left, busier to the right).
Save sound: keeps what you hear right now as a preset, in one tap.
Tap an icon to change tabs. The one you\'re on shows its name.
Sound: your microphone and the effects.
The Band: rhythm, melodies and kits.
Realms: sounds that change to fit where you are.
Scenes: other sound worlds to load.
Put your headphones on and press Start. You\'ll hear the room around you, with nothing added yet.
Tap the word Echo to open its card.
Drag Echo level up, then try Echo time and Echo feedback, wherever you like. Talk, clap or click your fingers: you\'ll hear your voice change while you move the sliders.
Hear it? Play as long as you like, then tap Next.

That's how every effect works: open its card, turn something up, listen.

When you tap Done, Echo goes back to where it was before the tour, so you start from a clean slate. Try one thing at a time and hear how each one answers you.
